Limit the stacked articulation to two major readings to preserve continuity.
Keep the upper mass calm and minimize visually colliding offsets.
Open the court further to make the public void legible.
Align the court opening to the access side to reinforce the entry threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the radial repetition with a calmer vertical hierarchy so the dominant court mass remains readable instead of fragmenting into repeated fins.
Reduce repetition to preserve one dominant gesture and avoid over-segmentation.
Introduce a bounded stacked profile rather than a rotating fan-like read, improving section continuity.
Enlarge the court so the void becomes a clearer public figure and better matches the neighborhood-living brief.
Keep the void aligned to the verified access side to strengthen the public threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact court mass with a clear carved void, but the visible four-view result is weakly resolved in section and too fragmented by the bend-plus-radial treatment. The dominant gesture is not fully stable across views: the top view shows a more legible tapered/bar-into-court form, while the perspective views read as a block with repetitive fin-like slicing and some awkward collisions/overlaps. The parcel is generally occupied, but the gesture does not strongly respond to the boundary as a coherent edge-to-void figure. The blue access edge is acknowledged only indirectly; the ground response is present but not strongly legible as an active public threshold. For neighborhood living, the mass can plausibly support the brief only at a basic level because it includes a courtyard, but the roof/section language feels more like an arbitrary sculpted object than a calm street building with clear hierarchy. Reference 1 and 2 are the most transferable for compact court organization and active threshold logic; reference 4 is only useful for general base/top hierarchy; reference 5 is a counterfactual about maintaining openness under a primary mass.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact massing with a protected inner court and clear perimeter-to-void hierarchy supports neighborhood-scale public/private gradation.
Layered edge conditions and a planted courtyard suggest an inhabitable ground threshold and usable outdoor room.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Small interior scale and simple edge carving can keep a modest commercial program legible at neighborhood scale.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower typology is only partially transferable; avoid copying the vertical emphasis.
